payload.body: # Release v5.24.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling 2 Mini Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's. A research checkpoint ([TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research)) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2_loop) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/) | [HF Blog Post](https://huggingface.co/blog/inkling2mini) * Add Inkling2 Mini (#51050) by @guarin ### Apertus 1.5 Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text. It extends the Apertus language model with the EMU3.5 vision tokenizer for images and WavTokenizer for audio. The EMU3.5 tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as Chameleon's, and it assigns codes by the largest inner product with the codebook. The media tokenizers turn images and audio into discrete tokens, which the language backbone processes alongside text in a shared input vocabulary. The output vocabulary contains only text tokens, so image and audio generation are not supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/apertus1p5) * Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft ### WavTokenizer WavTokenizer encodes 24 kHz mono audio into discrete tokens using a single codebook, at 40 or 75 tokens per second depending on the checkpoint, and reconstructs audio from those tokens. `WavTokenizerModel` encodes and decodes, and `WavTokenizerEncoderModel` only encodes. Speech, music/audio and unified checkpoints are available. The 40-token-per-second variant is the audio tokenizer of Apertus 1.5. Training the codec is not supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/wavtokenizer) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2408.16532) * Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft ### Dory Dory is a looped (latent-recurrent) language model from NVIDIA. It uses a normalized-GPT architecture with interleaved sliding-window and full attention layers. A shared block of layers is applied repeatedly, so Dory can spend more compute per token. The loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/dory) | [Paper (nGPT)](https://huggingface.co/papers/2410.01131) * Add Dory model support (#50099) by @shan18 ### HY4-VL HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) combines the HYV4 mixture-of-experts text backbone with a vision encoder for image-text and video-text generation. It supports dynamic-resolution visual inputs and uses multimodal rotary position embeddings (mRoPE) to represent temporal and spatial positions. It builds on the Qwen2-VL design and shares its vision patch merger with HunYuan-VL. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/hy_v4_vl) * Add HY4-VL (#50877) by @vasqu ### Omnilingual ASR Omnilingual ASR is a suite of multilingual speech-recognition models from Meta FAIR that covers more than 1,600 languages. Each model pairs a Wav2Vec2-style audio encoder with one of two heads: * **CTC** (`OmniASRForCTC`): a linear projection to the vocabulary, decoded non-autoregressively with greedy CTC. * **Audio language model** (`OmniASRForConditionalGeneration`): audio embeddings are projected into a Llama decoder that generates the transcription. It optionally takes a language code (e.g. `"eng_Latn"`), which generally improves transcription quality. Both variants come in 300M, 1B, 3B and 7B sizes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/omniasr) | [CTC Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/omniasr_ctc) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.09690) * Adding Omnilingual ASR models (#43265) by @ebezzam ### Lara Mini Lara Mini is a multilingual base language model from Translated with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters per token. It is a hybrid of linear-time recurrent layers, sliding-window attention and a few global attention layers, each followed by a fine-grained mixture of experts. The weights are released under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license (non-commercial use) in a gated repository. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lara_mini) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.16956) * Add Lara Mini (#50819) by @ValeGian ### SarvamMLA SarvamMLA is the architecture of Sarvam-105B, a 105B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model from Sarvam AI. It combines Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with sparse MoE routing: 128 routed experts with 8 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. It uses sigmoid routing with group-based top-k selection and YaRN rotary embeddings for contexts up to 131K tokens. The architecture is the same as DeepSeek-V3, with a custom configuration. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/sarvam_mla) * Add SarvamMLA model (sarvamai/sarvam-105b) (#44569) by @aashay-sarvam ### SarvamMoE SarvamMoE is the architecture of Sarvam-30B, Sarvam AI's 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It uses grouped-query attention with QK normalization, and 128 routed experts with 6 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. The architecture is the same as GLM-4-MoE, so the auto classes load it with the GLM-4-MoE implementation and only `SarvamMoEConfig` is specific to SarvamMoE. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/sarvam_moe) * Add SarvamMoE (sarvamai/sarvam-30b) (#51023) by @hmellor ### EXAONE EXAONE covers the EXAONE 3.0, EXAONE 3.5 and EXAONE Deep language models from LG AI Research. Their architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load them with `LlamaModel` and `LlamaForCausalLM`, and only `ExaoneConfig` is specific to EXAONE. The released checkpoints are renamed to the Llama names when loading and back when saving, so they no longer need `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/exaone) * Add EXAONE (#50966) by @hmellor ### Model updates * **Ling 3.1 Flash** now loads natively through `BailingHybrid`, like Ling 3.0 in v5.20.0 (#49737) by @icavan * **Beam** gains a `BeamForTokenClassification` head (#50634) by @AymenKallala ## Breaking changes ### Cache renaming: `past_key_values` / `cache_params` → `cache` (#50585, #50730) `past_key_values` and `cache_params` are renamed to `cache` across the library. The old names still work with a deprecation warning; see the dedicated section below. * 🚨🚨 Rename `past_key_values`/`cache_params` to `cache` (#50585) by @Cyrilvallez * Bump minimal peft version for cache name compatibility (#50730) by @Cyrilvallez Attention models used to call their cache `past_key_values`, while Mamba-style and linear-attention models called it `cache_params`. Hybrid models therefore had to juggle two names for the same object. There is now a single name, `cache`, everywhere: model `forward` signatures, `generate`, `prepare_inputs_for_generation`, the masking utilities, and every `ModelOutput`. ```python # Before outputs = model(input_ids, past_key_values=past_key_values, use_cache=True) next_cache = outputs.past_key_values # Now outputs = model(input_ids, cache=cache, use_cache=True) next_cache = outputs.cache ``` * **Fully backward compatible for now**: `past_key_values=` / `cache_params=` are renamed to `cache` automatically, with a one-time deprecation warning. Model `forward` and `prepare_inputs_for_generation` accept the old names until **v5.40.0**, and `generate` accepts them until **v6.0.0**. Passing both an old name and `cache` raises a `ValueError`. * **Outputs too**: `outputs.past_key_values`, `outputs.cache_params` and `outputs["past_key_values"]` still return the cache. Output classes can also still be built with the old field names (e.g. `CausalLMOutputWithPast(past_key_values=...)`), so most remote-code models keep working unchanged. * **Custom code**: models defined outside the library should rename their arguments to `cache`. Layers now call `cache.update(key_states, value_states, layer_idx, kwargs=kwargs)`, so custom `Cache` subclasses that override `update` should accept the extra `kwargs` argument. 🚨 `peft>=0.22.0` is now required. 📚 Docs: ### Multimodal Outputs Generative multimodal models now return shared output classes (`MultimodalBaseModelOutputWithPast`, `MultimodalCausalLMOutputWithPast`, and their MoE variants) instead of one output class per model. Code that checks for a model-specific output class should switch to these. * 🚨 Multimodal Model Output for generative LMs (#50379) by @zucchini-nlp `modeling_attn_mask_utils.py` has been removed. Every function in it had been deprecated in favor of `transformers.masking_utils`. Remote-code models that still import `_prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask` or `AttentionMaskConverter` from it must move to `transformers.masking_utils`. ### Other things * Remove deprecated and unused older mask API file (#50728) by @Cyrilvallez LayoutLMv3 (and the PP-DocLayoutV2 reading-order model that shares its code) now go through the attention interface, so SDPA and flex attention are supported. The relative position bias is built once per forward pass and passed to attention as `position_bias`. * 🚨 LayoutLMv3: support SDPA through the attention interface, build the relative position bias once (#50688) by @14H034160212 ## Cache Beyond the rename, this release adds static-cache support to assisted decoding and fixes `generate` with flex attention and a static cache. `StaticCache` now allocates values with the value states' dtype, and the cache is kept under activation checkpointing when gradients are off. The `is_linear` / `is_croppable` properties are fixed for hybrid linear/full-attention models, BigBird block-sparse decoding works with a KV cache, and KV sharing is restored for the Gemma 4 assistants. * Support static cache in assisted decoding (#49415) by @jiqing-feng * Simplify cache handling in generate (#50910) by @Cyrilvallez * Fix generate with flex attention and a static cache (#50864) by @tarekziade * Allocate the StaticCache values with the value states' dtype (#49554) by @qgallouedec * Keep the cache under activation checkpointing when gradients are off (#50890) by @qgallouedec * [cache] Fix is_linear property to correctly remove hybrid layers (#51030) by @Cyrilvallez * Fix is_croppable property for mixed linear-full attention classes (#51028) by @Cyrilvallez * Fix BigBird block-sparse decoding with a KV cache (#49984) by @jiqing-feng * fix(gemma4): Restore KV sharing for the Gemma 4 assistants and their targets (#50531) by @harshaljanjani * Fix Dory vocabulary resizing, loop validation, and last-loop static caching (#50982) by @shan18 * Fix device placement in `test_bc_cache_name_{forward,generate}` (#50757) by @ydshieh * Update test_dynamic_cache_hard expected values for A10G (#50822) by @ydshieh ## Generation Generation fixes cover sampled beam search (candidates are sorted again before finalization), constrained sampling (batch IDs are preserved), `generate` on MPS with encoder-decoder models, and `TextStreamer`, which no longer drops spaces or lags on text without spaces such as Chinese, Japanese and Korean. `StopStringCriteria` initializes faster, and its cache now actually hits. * Restore sorting of sampled beam candidates before finalization (#50754) by @BlazeSR10hawk * fix(generate): preserve batch IDs in constrained sampling (#50883) by @BlazeSR10hawk * Fix generate for mps and encoder-decoder models (#51032) by @Cyrilvallez * Fix TextStreamer dropping spaces sometimes (#51036) by @Cyrilvallez * Fix long lagging when streaming text without spaces and NJK chars (#36708) by @CNSeniorious000 * Speed up StopStringCriteria init and fix its cache never hitting (#50780) by @TheNetherWatcher ## Continuous batching Continuous batching now works under `torch.inference_mode()` and finds sharded key/value projections under any decoder path. The per-token memory estimate scales with the TP size, warmup handles async and static inputs correctly, and an out-of-bounds error in the top-k processor is fixed. * [CB] Scale the per-token memory estimate by the TP size (#48566) by @qgallouedec * Continuous batching: find the sharded key/value projections under any decoder path (#50366) by @qgallouedec * Fix continuous batching under torch.inference_mode() (#50863) by @tarekziade * [CB] Re-order the warmup block so async warms both sets of inputs (#50868) by @remi-or * Wait for each warmup forward before the next one rewrites the static inputs (#50353) by @qgallouedec * Fix out-of-bounds error in continuous batching top-k processor (#50282) by @khush-patel-09 * [CB] Replace test prompts with less ambiguous ones (#50876) by @remi-or ## Chat templates, parsing and serving Chat parsing gets a new `python-call-list` content parser, better handling of bare keys and duplicate XML arguments, and three further parser fixes. `apply_chat_template` accepts message objects, and assistant masks are correct with left truncation. `transformers serve` handles a missing Hub cache, lists loaded models in `/v1/models`, keeps local paths containing `@`, and keeps assistant content when `tool_calls` is empty. * [Chat Parsing] Add `python-call-list` content parser (#50619) by @nico-martin * [Chat Parsing] Quote bare keys that have whitespace around them with `unquoted_keys` (#50917) by @gagan-baghel * [Chat Parsing] Preserve array values when merging duplicate XML arguments (#50760) by @crunz-ailab * Fix three chat parsing bugs (#50655) by @Rocketknight1 * Fix apply_chat_template with message objects (#50818) by @Rocketknight1 * Fix assistant tokens mask with left truncation (#50758) by @yibol9768-alt * fix(chat templating): isolate concurrent assistant tracking (#50673) by @BlazeSR10hawk * Just a small improvement in jinja (#50635) by @zucchini-nlp * Accept argument types in parentheses in get_json_schema docstrings (#50745) by @miinimal * [serve] Handle missing Hub cache and include loaded models in /v1/models (#50663) by @RyanMullins * [serve] Preserve local model paths containing '@' in ModelManager (#50662) by @RyanMullins * [serve] Keep assistant content when tool_calls is null or empty (#50707) by @AabhasK ## Pipelines Multimodal pipelines now accept media-only inputs and string assistant prefills, keep Mistral prefills in Voxtral, stop mutating generation kwargs, and return chat messages as `input_text` when returning tensors. `pipeline` also respects a `device_map` that targets a single device. * fix(pipelines): support media-only inputs in AnyToAnyPipeline (#50856) by @BlazeSR10hawk * fix(pipelines): support string assistant prefill in multimodal full-t… (#50679) by @BlazeSR10hawk * fix: preserve Mistral prefill in Voxtral and multimodal pipelines (#50624) by @BlazeSR10hawk * fix(pipelines): avoid mutating multimodal generation kwargs (#50786) by @BlazeSR10hawk * Return the chat messages as input_text when multimodal pipelines return tensors (#50816) by @burrows99 * Fix `pipeline` ignoring `device_map` when it targets a single device (#50645) by @wanhakim ## Vision Vision fixes cover Muse Glimmer's embedding order, GotOCR2 and Emu3 image sizes, Kimi video inputs, NemotronH Omni video forwarding, SAM3 RoPE precision in bf16, and DETR-family configs with `dilation=None`. SigLIP2 and LFM2-VL now process all images at once with tensor ops. Flash Attention is turned off for multimodal models whose image mask it would drop. * Fix Muse Glimmer vision embedding order (#50847) by @sid-rp * Fix GotOCR2 image size (#50810) by @guarin * Fix Emu3 image sizes after channel format conversion (#50615) by @stefanielizeth73-art * Kimi video fix (#50633) by @zucchini-nlp * Fix NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3 video forwarding and MTP vision norm weight conversion (#49839) by @meatybobby * Keep SAM3's RoPE positions in fp32 when loading in bf16 (#50938) by @qgallouedec * Fix loading DETR-family configs that store dilation=None (#50934) by @sibisrinivasb * SigLIP2: compute the position-embedding resize for all images with tensor ops (#50736) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * LFM2-VL: run the projector on all images at once (#50734) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * LFM2-VL: integration expectations after #50734 (A10, MI300X) (#50923) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * Turn off Flash Attention support for multimodal models whose image mask it drops (#50724) by @albertvillanova ## Audio Audio fixes cover the OmniASR CTC blank token, Qwen3 Omni audio kwargs, Qwen3-ASR's `truncation=False` default, PeAudioVideo loading with timm 1.0.31, and the audio training examples. * Fix OmniASR CTC blank token ID (#51040) by @taking-lying-flat * Add missing past_key_values deprecation decorator to OmniASRForCondit… (#50983) by @RyanMullins * Fix Qwen3 Omni audio kwargs forwarding (#50616) by @remote-controlled-man * Restore `truncation=False` default for Qwen3-ASR audio (#50740) by @hmellor * Fixes PeAudioVideo model loading with timm 1.0.31. In that version, t… (#50862) by @sywangyi * FIx audio training examples. (#50672) by @ebezzam ## Quantization Dequantized models are now saved without the quantizer's weight conversions, and the unquantized weights of a dequantized FP8 checkpoint are cast to the model's dtype. The quantization docs also get a standard template for each method. * Save dequantized models without the quantizer's weight conversions (#50271) by @qgallouedec * Cast the unquantized weights of a dequantized FP8 checkpoint to the model's dtype (#50595) by @qgallouedec * Update inkling2 quant config (#50829) by @guarin * [docs] Standard template for quantization methods (#50848) by @stevhliu ## Parallelization FSDP2 modules are resharded before the optimizer is created, pipeline parallelism spreads layers more evenly, and TP sharding of tied weights is fixed. * Reshard FSDP2 modules before creating the optimizer (#50535) by @qgallouedec * [perf] Spread layer over PP more evenly (#50693) by @francesco-bertolotti * Fixes an issue related to TP sharding of tied weights (#50272) by @tengomucho ## Exporters Exported ONNX, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch programs load without `trust_remote_code`. Pickled `.pt2` programs, which can run arbitrary code when loaded, now require `trust_remote_code=True`. * Exporters: ONNX, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch programs load without trust_remote_code (#50886) by title: Meta premieres India’s First Government-Led Microdrama Series on Scams Awareness
summary: Meta has partnered with The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (MIB), Prasar Bharati, Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to launch India’s first government-led public interest microdrama series on online scams. The series will premiere on Instagram and will soon be available on Waves OTT. The “Scam se Bacho” microdrama will be Waves OTT’s inaugural series with Meta that aims to educate audiences on some of the most prevalent online scams today, including fake job offers , investment and digital arrest scams, reiterating the importance of reporting suspicious behaviour online and encouraging users to call the national cybercrime helpline 1930 in case of fraud. Through an engaging, social-first approach, this initiative builds on the growing popularity of microdramas and demonstrates how innovative storytelling formats can be harnessed to make important public interest information more accessible and relatable. Scam Se Bacho: Raising Awareness Through A Whole-Of-Society Approach Building on Meta’s flagship anti-scam campaign “Scam se Bacho” – this latest initiative expands our educational efforts and reinforces the importance of tackling online scams through a whole-of-society approach by bringing together government agencies, creators and industry partners to reach audiences through India’s fastest-growing storytelling format.

title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
summary: Customers increasingly self-host large language models (LLMs) on GPUs for control over cost, accuracy, and latency. However, self-hosting often means paying for redundant GPU work because small, isolated caches on each server can’t hold or share the growing context AI agents and chat applications resend. Consider a legal AI assistant that can accumulate hundreds of thousands of tokens of case history in each conversation. When a lawyer returns to a thread after lunch, responses from the LLM can take minutes. The GPU server that picks up the request has none of that history in its memory. So, the GPU recomputes the key-value (KV) attention states for all of those tokens, a step called prefill, before it writes a word. The same pattern slows down resumed coding agents, agentic AI assistants, and document Q&A assistants. Distributed KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache can cut self-hosted LLM inference costs by up to 40% and time to first token (TTFT) by up to 80%. title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm
summary: Keeping a shared Slurm cluster for foundation model development in sync entails keeping several separately maintained pieces of configuration matched to what’s running on the nodes. The cluster’s shape lives on multiple configuration files, its software in custom scripts, its network topology in files that must be edited as nodes change, and its users in a roster that an administrator must maintain and rerun. Over time these pieces drift away from what’s actually running, and nothing tells you when they do. We believe cluster configurations should be managed the way you manage the rest of your AWS infrastructure. You declare what you want through an API or the console, AWS validates it before it’s applied, the cluster is kept in that state continuously, and you can see whether it’s working. During 2026, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod brought that approach to Slurm clusters, with API-driven Slurm configuration, AMI-based configuration, continuous provisioning, automatic topology management, and deep health checks. Today, we launched cluster extensions, which bring the same approach to the software and settings on running nodes, with managed extensions for observability and user management. title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters
summary: During a traffic peak, a request can sit in a queue on a saturated HyperPod cluster while GPUs on another cluster, sometimes in another AWS Region, sit idle. You have already paid for that capacity, but your requests can’t reach it. In Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway , we showed how the Inference Gateway gives each Amazon SageMaker HyperPod cluster a single, GPU-aware endpoint. It reads real-time signals such as key-value (KV) cache utilization and queue depth to place every request on the best-suited pod. That solves routing inside one cluster, but not across clusters. Today, SageMaker HyperPod introduces the Global Inference Gateway. It is one SageMaker-managed gateway that routes across every cluster you register, in one Region or across Regions. The gateway picks the cluster and carries the request over the AWS backbone, with automatic failover and authentication through AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Inside each cluster, the Inference Gateway keeps picking the pod, unchanged. The Global Inference Gateway is the second tier of the architecture we described in part 1. Proving, one use case at a time, that AI systems follow it is another. Every new generative AI application adds one more system to prove. Teams can now build one in days, but each still needs a risk committee’s approval before it reaches customers or employees. When that approval depends on reviewers reading documents and testing the system by hand, governance becomes the slowest step in the pipeline. Standard Bank Group chose to automate that proof. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank deployed an automated assessment that scores each generative AI use case against international AI standards and its own policies. The assessment produces reports and a dashboard that show what is already in place, what is working well, and what still needs mitigation. This post explains how the assessment runs on AWS and what Standard Bank Group learned from its first runs. title: Announcing Amazon Textract Insights: Verifiable generative AI for documents
summary: Organizations across financial services, insurance, healthcare, and the public sector depend on document processing. They turn scanned files and paper forms into structured data their systems can act on. As generative AI has matured, these organizations want more than accurate text extraction. They want to describe the information they need in their own words and get dependable, auditable answers from complex documents. Today, we are announcing the general availability of Amazon Textract Insights , a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract available through a new API within Amazon Textract. With Amazon Textract Insights, you describe the fields you want in natural language and submit a document or a mixed, multi-document packet. You receive structured results in which each value carries a confidence score and page-level grounding, with no model training required. The challenge of extracting data from mixed packets Many of the high-value document workloads involve diverse, mixed packets rather than clean, single-purpose files. title: Introducing enhanced infrastructure observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
summary: Large-scale model training is one of the most expensive workloads you can run on GPUs, and a single unhealthy accelerator can stall an entire distributed job. When training throughput drops, the hard part is rarely noticing that something is wrong. It is figuring out why and where. Teams often spend hours or days sifting through logs and disconnected dashboards to decide whether a slowdown came from a throttled GPU, a saturated network link, or a stalled data pipeline on the host. Today, we are announcing enhanced observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, a new capability that helps you diagnose GPU training issues faster. It brings together diagnostic and profiling capabilities for training workloads that run on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and Slurm orchestrators: Diagnostic summary uses Amazon CloudWatch’s DetectGroupOutliers API to compare each GPU in a training job on utilization, memory, temperature, power, and SM clock, and flags GPUs that deviate from their peers. title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
summary: When hundreds of agents serve thousands of developers, enterprise governance can’t be an afterthought. At the BMW Group’s R&D, more than 12,500 developers work on approximately 500 million lines of vehicle software code. This software is augmented by the BMW Connected Vehicle backend, a cloud-based system of more than 1,300 microservices providing digital services for 24 million vehicles in the field. In regulated industry, the bar for (software) quality, stability, and governance compliance is exceptionally high. While research, frameworks, and guidelines now facilitate building agents, industrializing and operating high-quality agents in an efficient, scalable manner remains a significant challenge. Scaling agentic AI across a large organization cannot be achieved by isolated teams. It requires collective effort, locally driven experimentation, and active knowledge sharing across the enterprise. This creates a fundamental governance dichotomy: Development teams need the freedom to innovate rapidly, while the enterprise must enforce standards for safety, security, composability, and cost-efficiency. Without that balance, organizations risk a fragmented landscape of AI islands and costly duplicate work. This presents a real challenge given hundreds of globally distributed teams building agents across the BMW Group. title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
summary: Every inference endpoint is well tuned the day it goes into production. Teams choose an instance type, serving configuration, and scaling settings that suit the model and its traffic at launch. With the endpoint serving smoothly, they understandably move on to the next priority. The workload, however, rarely stays still. Traffic patterns evolve, prompts grow longer, serving engines such as vLLM ship new releases, SageMaker inference develops new optimization techniques, and new fine-tuned checkpoints change the resources your model needs. Over time, a well-tuned endpoint quietly drifts. Latency and time to first token edge upward. A configuration that was never quite ideal keeps missing available performance gains. A GPU provisioned for demand that never materialized sits idle week after week. Because nothing has failed, no alarm sounds, and the drift goes unnoticed until users feel it or the bill reflects it. Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors your generative AI inference endpoints and tells you when a change could improve performance or lower cost by using Generative AI optimized inference recommendations feature with Agentic experience in SageMaker JupyterLab . title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
summary: For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions? Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria to give candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. Decades of research in industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology have shown that structured interviews help organizations evaluate candidates and predict job performance (Schmidt & Hunter, 1998; Sackett et al., 2022). Yet delivering structured interviews at scale requires significant time and expertise to develop competencies, create q uestions, train interviewers, and evaluate responses consistently . Amazon Connect Talent brings established hiring science to AI-led interviews at scale. Connect Talent uses structured questions, adaptive follow-ups, and evidence-based scoring to help organizations gather consistent, job-related information while giving more candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their strengths. We built Connect Talent around three core design principles and evaluated how well the service applies them through a combination of internal research and independent expert review. AgentCore harness also introduces lifecycle hooks, so you can apply your own deterministic checks and notifications at defined points in the agent loop. With this upgrade, agents that rely on the managed defaults get a recommended model, a task-oriented system prompt, automatic prompt caching (initially for Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock), and proactive context management. They also get additional built-in tools for planning, web retrieval, filesystem access, context offloading, and task delegation. This gives agents greater capabilities during long tasks, allowing them to keep track of subtasks, reduce context window usage, and delegate work. With hooks, you can transform non-deterministic AI behavior into predictable, safe, and governed workflows by running deterministic code at specific lifecycle checkpoints. title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
summary: As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock , token spend often grows even as per-token prices fall. Without cost allocation tags in place, your cloud invoice shows AI spend as a single line item rather than by team, workload, agent, or model. Cheaper tokens expand adoption, and agentic workloads multiply invocations. As successful AI use cases scale, consumption can rise faster than unit prices drop. The economic question is whether the business value generated grows faster than the cost of the intelligence required to produce it. The Linux Foundation has launched the Tokenomics Foundation to develop open standards for AI cost economics, a sign that managing the economics of AI is now an industry discipline. In this post, you will learn about six levers for optimizing token spend, how Accenture applied them in production, and how to apply them using Amazon Bedrock. Accenture applied these levers in four client engagements across telecom, insurance, mining, and a large enterprise deployment. The same levers are available natively on Amazon Bedrock as described in this post. Where savings were measured, token spend fell by about 40–85 percent. Results are specific to each client’s workload and may vary. Client names are withheld by Accenture

title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
summary: Serving a model from more than one AWS Region is a well-established pattern for highly available inference: when one Region runs short of GPU capacity, requests move to another. The pattern is simple to describe and hard to operate. Until now, if you served models on Amazon SageMaker AI managed endpoints, cross-Region routing was a piece you still had to build yourself. Today, we’re introducing cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI. It uses a new resource, the inference router, that gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. You register the destinations that serve a model, and your application invokes the router instead of a specific endpoint. The router keeps requests in its own Region while the local destination is healthy, shifts new requests to another registered destination when it isn’t, and returns traffic gradually after recovery. In this post, we explain how cross-Region inference routing decides where each request runs, walk through an example with one model in two Regions, and cover monitoring, limits, and what you pay. title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. title: 重控制、轻渲染，达瓦科技的 AI 视频工业路线
summary: 头图来源：极客公园 今年以来，视频生成模型的进步肉眼可见，AI 短剧、换脸、场景合成在各个平台越来越多，但一个现实问题始终存在：生成一条满意的视频，往往要反复「抽卡」，算力和时间成本都不低；而一旦进入专业影视管线，今天的模型能承担的工业级工作仍然有限。 关于这个问题，行业有两种思路。一种堆参数、扩算力，相信通用大模型终会跨过工业门槛；另一种扎进真实片场，从具体需求自下而上生长。达瓦科技走的是后一条路径。 达瓦科技总部位于重庆永川，团队从 2014 年开始运营科技影视片场，2023 年成立达瓦科技，转向 AI 模型，今年已连续完成 Pre-A 轮、A 轮融资，累计融资约 5 亿元人民币。 他们选择的路线是「重控制、轻渲染」：自研控制层基座模型 Latent Stage，把对人物、动作、镜头、灯光、场景的理解和控制单独做成一层，再交给渲染层出画面。围绕这条路线，公司有两款产品：面向专业内容团队、做离线生成的 FilmOS，以及在单张消费级显卡上就能实时运行的世界模型 Scenes AI。 这套架构的底气来自数据。达瓦在真实片场中积累了约 180TB 的结构化「过程数据」，记录的不只是成片画面，还有从剧本、机位、灯光到动作捕捉的完整拍摄过程。 以下为极客公园创始人张鹏与达瓦科技 CTO 朱子威和 CPO 李宗兴对谈实录，由极客公园整理。 01 从科技片场出发，做「控制层」 张鹏： 过去一年视频生成模型进步很快，大家都能刷到 AI 短剧，很多人也开始自己生成视频玩。但成本一直很高，对算力需求大，真正放进专业影视工业，能发挥多少作用，还是个问题。 今天我们就看看，在主流的视频大模型之外，有没有别的技术路线。先请宗兴介绍一下达瓦科技。 李宗兴： 达瓦科技最早是一家科技影视公司。可以讲个故事：1975 年卢卡斯想拍《星球大战》，发现很多电影技术实现不了，就创办了工业光魔，专门去解决这些技术问题。需求会推动技术发展，就像游戏玩家推动了 GPU 的进步。 我们的片场经常给技术团队提真实的问题，比如导演只想改画面里的一小部分，为什么要重新拍整个镜头？能不能只保留这个人物、这个动作，只改其他部分？在这些需求推动下，我们走向了控制层，做一个控制层基座模型，让视频真正可编辑、可理解。 我们有两款核心产品。一款是 FilmOS ，一个 AI Agent 影视创作平台，基于一句话的目标就能生成高质量画面，得益于控制模型，它可以让你少抽卡就能拿到合适的画面。另一款是正在研发的实时世界模型 Scenes AI ，基于稀疏扩散自回归架构和世界模型，能把摄像头画面实时演化、编辑，是一个 Physical AI 产品。公司财务口径上，我们一年的 ARR 大概在 1 亿美元左右。 张鹏： 收入很可观。你们本质上是在控制层做模型，解决的就是「少抽卡」——哪不行就局部改，不用整条重拍。 02 控制层像导演，渲染层像相机 张鹏： 「少抽卡」的目标，要用什么技术实现？你们的架构和路线是什么？ 朱子威： 先分层看。渲染层像相机，负责把画面拍出来，渲染层越好，画面效果越好，比如英伟达的 DLSS 5，用神经网络把老游戏渲染出很真实的效果，对应视频模型里的 DiT 扩散部分。控制层更像导演，决定场景里有哪些物体、演员从哪走到哪、有什么道具和交互、时序上怎么变化。 渲染层像相机，控制层像导演。 可以把它理解成一个虚拟空间，里面的桌子、凳子、人物、机位都真实存在，只是肉眼看不见。控制层根据导演的需求把这些要素匹配进去，再把结果交给渲染层，得到一个不用再花大力气修改的结果。它符合真实物理环境下该有的拍摄逻辑，也不会出现抽卡常见的穿帮——比如人走过去一扭头，门口的人突然坐到沙发上了。 张鹏： 这里有个关键区别：你们是一个基座模型，不是一个视频 Agent。这两者怎么理解？ 朱子威： Agent 解决的是信息差。很多人拿到视频模型不会用，会写提示词、懂升格、推拉摇移、zoom in/zoom out 这些术语的人，结果就能逼近模型上限，Agent 是帮人补上这个信息差。控制层解决的是认知差：模型能不能理解一个完整的物理片场。 Agent 解决信息差，控制层解决认知差。 张鹏： 比如这盏灯突然灭了，空间里会发生哪些连锁反应，这就是认知。我调暗一个灯光，这一个输入应该带来一串输出的变化。 朱子威： 对。Agent 遇到这种情况，可能会重新生成一堆图片，再想办法交给视频模型，中间走很多弯路，每次处理都在增加不必要的信息熵，最后拿不到高维认知下直接控制的结果。控制层是在渲染之前就把这些问题解决掉，像一个全知的导演助手，在你花大价钱渲染之前先把事办好。 03 多一层计算，为什么反而更省钱 张鹏： 搞基座模型肯定要花钱。作为一家做模型的公司，现在融资情况怎么样，有多少弹药？ 李宗兴： 我们最近连续完成了 A 轮和 Pre-A 轮融资，大概 5 亿元人民币。现阶段肯定够用，因为我们训的不是特别大的模型，而是控制基座。在我们看来，控制层会革新内容形态的交互，是特别值得投入的方向。 张鹏： 投资人主要看重什么？ 李宗兴： 核心有两点。第一，我们有真实业务收入，不是完全靠外部融资推动，商业飞轮已经在转，我们不是一家还在找 AI 场景的公司。 第二，我们在解决影视行业的真实需求：现在做任何小修改都要重新生成整个画面，而我们用局部控制大幅降低抽卡次数。行业往往只算单次生成的成本，但水下有很多隐性成本——一个镜头到底要抽多少次卡？把抽卡次数降下来，才是真正降低影视生产的成本。 另外，我们能基于一张消费级显卡做实时内容，比如把会议室铺满海浪、把衣服实时换成汉服或钢铁侠。如果要靠数百万、上千万的 GPU 集群实现，就没有经济适用性；一张一两万的显卡能做到，落地的可能性就很大。未来还能把画面推到 AR 眼镜里，整个房间都能被重新渲染。 张鹏： 你们衡量的不是单次抽卡成本，而是完成一次有效交付的系统成本。那我再问一个技术问题：你们等于在原有模型之外又加了一层，为什么两层运算反而更划算？ 朱子威： 首先是一致性。控制层让结果更符合创作意图，大家抽卡时其实每 15 秒镜头画面质感都不差，问题是 60 分钟、100 分钟之后，内容不按你的方向走，我们的可控，是在完整内容的一致、可控 其次是精准度。做出来之后，我要改怎么办，渲染层是一坨像素，改掉这个杯子，重新生成就全乱了。我们控制层，能实现指哪打哪，其他要素完全不变。 大家说的抽卡，本质是「不可控」。通过我们的控制模型，原来要抽十次、二十次，现在三到四次，总体成本能下降 50%—60%。 张鹏： 就像便宜炮弹要打一万发才能炸掉碉堡，而一发精准制导导弹虽然贵，总体账反而更划算。 李宗兴： 对，就是精准制导。 张鹏： 再聊聊数据。你们做控制模型，数据是怎么来的？什么数据对这个模型最重要？ 朱子威： 主流视频模型更像用眼睛看视频学炒菜，我们的过程数据是真正「进过厨房」。一个电影级片场，从怎么备菜、选料、用什么厨具、什么火候，全部能量化。 我们会把片场里所有要素的状态——摄影机画面、机位、灯光、道具摆放、场务移动——放在同一时间轴上记录，很多硬件上打了信标、有专用跟踪设施，还用英伟达 Omniverse 搭建仿真环境，本质是数字孪生。自研的无标记动捕也起了很大作用。 张鹏： 就是把拍片从剧本到成片的全过程，全部向量化。 朱子威： 对，全部记录下来，再做大量仿真和变体。真实项目数量有限，我们就通过仿真和剧本调整去扩展数据，一生二、二生三，最后拿去做控制。 李宗兴： 我们的模型不是拿 LLM 改的，LLM 只是很小的部分。它按要素组拆解片场，人物动作、镜头、灯光每个要素都有专门的专家，整体是一个 MoE。模型 34B 参数，每个专家权重差距不大，因为几乎没有纯像素数据，数据压缩做得比较好，在剧集和非超大制作的动作戏范围内，已经展现出很强的控制力。 张鹏： 这个数据飞轮具体怎么转？ 李宗兴： 我们的片场从 2014 年做到现在，下一阶段它的定位会从收入来源变成一个「数据工厂」，把制片过程沉淀成世界模型的训练数据。 现在已经有 180TB 结构化的世界状态数据，训练出基座模型，再通过 FilmOS、Scenes AI 回到真实生产，生产又持续产生新数据，这是达瓦独特的商业飞轮。 我们还采购了英伟达 Omniverse 和 Cosmos 的企业授权，批量生成带物理约束的仿真数据，比如火焰怎么蔓延、种子怎么长成大树、积雪怎么融成水。 04 不是垂直模型，是通向 Physical AI 的世界模型 张鹏： 当年大模型落地时，有一派讲「垂直模型」。投资人会不会也问你们，这是不是个垂直模型？ 朱子威： 控制层并不只能用于视频生成。今年我们在苏州和英伟达方面做过很长的闭门沟通，结论是控制层是通向 Physical AI 不可或缺的部分，它本身有泛化性，只是我们现在的数据集偏垂直。偏垂直的好处是先在一个领域打出可用性和商业价值，反过来证明这条路是对的。 张鹏： 所以它不是垂直模型，更像世界模型的一种，代表对世界逻辑关系的理解，未来甚至能用于机器人训练。你们现在聚焦片场，是因为算力有限，先把一点打穿、做到正向利润。 朱子威： 对，什么都做等于什么都不做。先把一点打穿，拿到实打实的商业回报。 张鹏： 宗兴，主流做视频大模型的人相信只要持续 scaling，这些问题都能解决。你们是本来就在产业里的人，片场真实的痛点是什么？ 李宗兴： 片场每天都会提一些当下技术看似解决不了的问题。 比如一个一镜到底的长镜头，整体都很好，只出现一个小瑕疵，导演说「再保一条」，这一条就是经费在燃烧。这正是把我们推向控制端的原因——对一个镜头做局部修改。 再比如一盏灯从面前移过，不只是改一个灯光参数，它会让所有人脸的明暗、对比都发生变化，所以我们加了大量 Physical AI 的物理约束。观众判断画面真假，往往就看空间关系和物理细节对不对。 张鹏： 任何技术领域都有客户需求带来的「不可能三角」。你们的不可能三角是什么？ 朱子威： 是算力预算、生成时间、分辨率或质量，三者要取舍。 李宗兴： 客户经常问，能不能在手机上跑？我们的模型 34B、单次激活 4B，为了实时和低算力已经做了大量取舍。传统扩散模型计算下一帧要把整个画面重新算一遍，需要 GPU

title: 资本开支猛增 226%，AI 吞噬百亿利润：腾讯的 AI 故事，进入更重的阶段
summary: 头图来源：腾讯 腾讯的 AI 故事，正在进入一个有些沉重的阶段。 11 月 18 日，腾讯发布 2026 年第三季度财报。本季度营收 2073.4 亿元，同比增长 8%；Non-IFRS 经营利润 681 亿元，同比下降 6%；Non-IFRS 归母净利润 665 亿元，同比下降 6%。 图片来源：腾讯财报 本季度，腾讯资本开支达到 814 亿元，同比增长 527%，单季支出已经超过 2025 年全年；研发投入 323.6 亿元，同比增长 42%。大规模算力采购和预付款之下，自由现金流为负 691 亿元；若剔除算力采购预付款，自由现金流仍有 169 亿元。 单看收入，这依旧是一份稳健的财报。但把 AI 拆出来，曲线的分叉比上一季度更明显：若剔除混元、元宝、CodeBuddy、WorkBuddy、小微等新 AI 产品的收入、成本与开支，腾讯本季度 Non-IFRS 经营利润为 833 亿元，同比增长 8%，经营利润率 40%，和去年同期持平。 也就是说，老业务的盈利能力没有出问题，但新 AI 业务在这个季度对 Non-IFRS 经营利润造成了约 152 亿元的净影响，上一季度这个数字是 105 亿元。整体利润增速，就这样被拉到了负值区间。 腾讯把越来越多的当期现金，换成了 GPU、模型、Agent 和下一代入口。 一、「AI 折价」：152 亿口径差，和 814 亿的决心 先看整体经营情况。 三季度，腾讯营收 2073.36 亿元，同比增长 8%，环比增长 1%。三大板块里，营销服务收入 430 亿元，同比增长 19%，是增速最快的板块；金融科技及企业服务收入 637 亿元，增长 9%；增值服务收入 983 亿元，增长 3%。微信及 WeChat 合并月活账户数达到 14.49 亿。 利润端的数字就没那么好看了。按非国际财务报告准则，腾讯三季度经营利润 681 亿元，同比下降 6%；IFRS 口径下经营利润 591 亿元，同比下降 7%。Non-IFRS 净利润 665 亿元，同样下滑 6%。 若剔除新 AI 产品的贡献，三季度 Non-IFRS 经营利润为 833 亿元，同比增长 8%，经营利润率 40%，与去年同期持平。两个口径之间相差约 152 亿元。「新 AI 产品」，主要包括混元、元宝、CodeBuddy、WorkBuddy 和小微。 也就是说，拖累利润的是正在投入期的 AI 业务。 投入的力度可以用几个数字感受一下。 三季度腾讯资本开支总额达到 814 亿元，同比增长 527%，单季支出已经超过 2025 年全年；前三季度累计资本开支 1662 亿元，同比增长 179%，钱主要流向 IT 基础设施、数据中心和土地使用权。现金口径的资本开支付款为 651 亿元，同比增长 226%。研发投入 323.6 亿元，同比增长 42%；一般及行政开支同比增长 29% 至 441 亿元，若剔除研发开支，这项费用仅增长 2%，非 AI 开支的管控依然很紧。 现金流受到的冲击最猛。 三季度自由现金流为负 691 亿元。经营活动产生的现金净额只有 26 亿元，而资本开支、媒体内容、租赁负债三笔付款合计 717 亿元。腾讯解释，经营现金流里包含大额算力采购预付款，主要用于混元升级、WorkBuddy 推理和云客户需求；若剔除这笔预付款，自由现金流本应为正 169 亿元。 资金状况随之改变，6 月底还有 582 亿元净现金，9 月底变为 137 亿元净债务。官方解释，这主要由大额算力采购造成，投资组合中处置超过新增投资带来的 84 亿元净流入，只抵消了一部分。腾讯账上仍有 5257 亿元现金及定期存款，持有的上市、非上市投资合计约 9026 亿元。 股东回报方面，腾讯三季度回购约 1587 万股、耗资约 70 亿港元，回购股份已注销。 市场对此有不小分歧，多家券商在财报前下调了目标价，野村、瑞银等机构早早提示 AI 支出对利润率的压制；但花旗、美银、里昂等多数大行仍维持「买入」评级，核心理由是短期利润承压夯实的是长期竞争力。这本质上是一道时间题：投资者愿意等多久，取决于回款来得有多快。 二、年化 5 亿美元的 WorkBuddy 与削减支出的元宝 电话会上，刘炽平披露了 WorkBuddy 的收入数据，按过去七天的收入折算，WorkBuddy 年化收入已经超过 5 亿美元，是腾讯会议营收的两倍以上；三季度单季收入环比二季度增长超过 5 倍。 图片来源：腾讯 用户侧，WorkBuddy 日活突破 1000 万，每天消耗超过 100 万亿 token，按大语言模型 token 消耗量计，已是国内第一的 AI 应用。 企业端的渗透上，企业版今年 6 月推出，中国百强企业里已有 60% 成为客户，中国企业 500 强覆盖率达到

title: 关于混元 4 模型、算力、刷榜与 RSI，姚顺雨回应一切
summary: 头图来源：ChatGPT 生成 11 月 21 日凌晨，腾讯首席 AI 科学家、混元大模型负责人姚顺雨和混元团队的研究员现身 Reddit LocalLLaMA 社区，开启了混元团队史上第一场面向全球开发者的公开 AMA。 图片来源：x 两小时内，姚顺雨和混元团队解答了 300 余条开发者提问，从底层架构取舍到长期路线规划，从量化落地经验到开源生态适配，几乎覆盖了当前开源大模型领域所有核心争议与关切。 过去不到一个月，混元刚刚完成一轮高密度产品发布——11 月 4 日推出的 Hy4 首次跻身全球最强开源模型之列，拿下 Agent Arena 开源模型榜首、Artificial Analysis 中国模型第二的成绩；一周后，定位「极致性价比」的 Hy4 flash 快速跟进，单任务成本仅为 Hy4 的二十分之一，上线首日 Token 调用量便突破 50 万亿。 如果把时间倒回九个月前—— 今年 2 月，混元才刚刚完成预训练与强化学习基础设施的全面重建。从重建底座到连发两款标杆级模型，九个月、平均每两个月一个大版本的迭代速度，背后是「preview 先行、正式版跟进」的闭环研发逻辑：把真实业务场景的反馈直接注入研发链路，在解决实际问题中完成能力跃迁。 模型路线上，团队走的是双线并行的思路，既相信规模化的潜力，会继续训练更大的模型探索能力上限；也同步布局小尺寸模型与端侧场景，试图在能力、成本与速度之间找到更务实的平衡点。 落到具体技术选择上，无论是注意力机制选型、MoE 稀疏度设计，还是量化方案的取舍，团队的判断都锚定实验结果、硬件适配条件与实际部署效率，并未将参数规模或榜单分数作为核心决策标准。 对于当前的能力短板，团队也没有回避，称过度思考仍是后训练阶段的核心难题，创意写作与文本可读性还有提升空间，递归自我改进相关技术尚处于早期摸索阶段。 此外，问答也覆盖了开发者普遍关心的实操问题，包括本地运行门槛、工具调用适配、开源生态合作进展；安全层面则提及了有害数据过滤、训练防护、红队评估等治理机制，同时坦言，模型的过度拒绝问题仍需进一步优化。 以下是极客公园从本次 Reddit AMA 中提炼出的核心问题，覆盖模型路线、技术架构、研发难点、开源生态等核心维度。 混元的整体产品路线是什么？接下来还有哪些新模型？ 混元采用「两端并行」的研发策略：一边扩大模型与数据规模，探索智能上限；一边压缩推理成本，主打极致性价比，Hy4 与 Hy4 flash 分别对应这两个方向。 后续产品路线清晰，更小尺寸的 Hy4-mini、Flash-Lite 模型已在规划中；24–31B 稠密模型正在评估；5–12B 级小型开源图像模型、新一代视频模型均在考虑范围内；循环式 MoE、持续学习等前沿方向也在积极研究。 不跟风 3T/5T 超大规模参数，混元对模型规模的判断是什么？ 团队认为，打磨扎实的小尺寸模型同样可以胜过大参数模型，且部署成本更低，研发过程中能沉淀更多技术经验。但混元同时相信 Scaling law 的有效性，下一代模型的参数量会显著扩大，会持续向更大规模投入研发。 Hy4 与 Hy4 flash 的架构核心差异在哪？关键取舍逻辑是什么？ Hy4 flash 继承了 Hy4 的 iHC、门控 MLA、DSA 技术底座，同时新增混合 SWA、LatentMoE、Engram 三大组件。 所有架构选择均围绕「性能-成本-硬件适配」的综合权衡：比如改用 SWA 替代门控 DSA，可将 KV cache 体积压缩至原有的 1/4，大幅降低服务成本；DSA 技术则解决了 MLA 解码阶段计算强度过高的问题，最终让团队在长期权衡后放弃 GQA、选择效果更优的 MLA。 此外，iHC、Engram 这类架构创新并非大模型专属，在小尺寸模型上能带来甚至更大的性能收益。 MoE 是不是越稀疏越好？极端稀疏路线为什么行不通？ 在激活参数量固定的前提下，提高稀疏度确实能提升计算效率；但如果保持总参数量不变、单纯降低激活参数，会显著损害模型质量——激活参数本质决定了计算预算，稀疏度的效率提升无法完全弥补计算量减少带来的能力损失。 对于数据中心部署，过于稀疏的 MoE 并不友好：会占用大量显存却无法充分利用算力，相同吞吐量下，不如运行总参数相当、激活参数更高的模型；端侧场景则会采用独立的架构-硬件协同设计思路。 端侧视觉模型的最小可用规模是多少？多模态有什么规划？ 针对图像推理、UI/图表理解等深度视觉任务（非单纯 OCR 或图像描述），团队验证，激活参数约 30 亿（A3B）级别的模型已经可以支撑相关能力。 多模态产品方面，团队正在考虑推出 5–12B 级别的小型开源图像模型，降低本地部署门槛，新一代混元视频模型也在推进中。 图片来源：reddit 后训练阶段最难解决的问题是什么？ 「过度思考」是后训练阶段最难改善的问题。 Hy4 为了追求极致智能，思维链偏长是已知问题；而 Hy4 flash 则通过强化学习专门控制了思维链长度，实现效率优先。 此外，长程智能体任务的强化学习落地中，最大挑战是环境漏洞导致的「奖励投机」，比如智能体通过搜索答案而非自主解题完成任务，需要反复修正环境规则与奖励机制。 MoE 量化如何避免能力退化？混元有哪些实操经验？ 团队沉淀了四点核心经验： 位宽分配上，down 投影因激活值存在离群值，对量化更敏感，会分配更多比特，位宽选择基于 Hessian 敏感度判断； 精度颗粒度上，更倾向按张量分配混合精度，而非按单个专家设置，避免破坏推理引擎的堆叠矩阵处理逻辑； 量化感知训练（QAT）中，路由器会和模型主体一起训练，避免路由漂移与工具调用能力退化； 方案优先级上，全参数 QAT 的模型质量优于 LoRA 类适配器方案，是团队的首选。 对标行业 AGI 分级，Hy4 处在什么水平？提升空间还有多大？ 团队自评 Hy4 处于 AGI 分级的 2.5 级水平，并明确表示 Hy4 远未到容量上限，在后训练层面仍有很大提升空间，目前正大规模投入强化学习技术，同时持续优化用户体验与模型安全性。 递归自我改进（RSI）进展如何？当前研发优先级怎么排？ 递归自我改进目前仍处于早期阶段，团队已开发若干内部基准用于评估核心能力。 但 RSI 并非当前最高优先级，团队现阶段的核心目标是打牢模型基础能力、提升通用智能水平，并与产品场景结合优化真实体验，而非优先推进模型自我迭代。 开源模型如何平衡安全能力与「过度拒绝」问题？ 安全层面，混元通过有害数据过滤、训练防护、红队评估三级机制推进负责任开源：网络安全方向重点训练防御性任务（漏洞分析、修复），过滤进攻性利用类数据。 团队同时承认，减少过度拒绝是重要的改进方向。根据内部评估，当前 Hy4 的漏洞发现能力较强，漏洞利用能力相对较弱。 本地部署的门槛有多高？开源生态适配进展如何？ 硬件门槛上，96GB 显存+128GB 系统内存即可运行 Hy4 flash，可将部分专家层、Engram 表卸载到主机内存降低显存压力。 生态适配方面，llama.cpp 适配正在推进，即将向社区发布；同时已与 vllm、sgl 等主流推理框架社区深度合作。 目前 Hy4 与 Hy4 flash 已可在 OpenCode、Claude Code、Cline 等开发工具中直接使用。 为什么不卷传统基准榜单？混元的评测理念是什么？ 混元坚持「评测真实性」原则，以真实任务而非榜单分数检验模型能力。 团队认为 GPQA、SWE-bench 等传统基准已出现分数饱和，参考价值下降，因此更倾向展示 Agent 编程、真实工程任务等高难度新基准的成绩。研发过程中不刻意刷榜，靠更丰富的训练数据、多样化的内部真实任务评测来打磨模型的实际可用性。

title: 黄仁勋遭董事会罢免主要原因曝光；《GTA6》首发收入 37.9 亿美元，超《复联 4》总票房；马斯克收到上海工厂员工特制边角料手办
summary: 《GTA6》首发收入达 37.9 亿美元，超越《复仇者联盟 4》总票房 Take-Two Interactive 表示，《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA6）的预购加上首发当日销售额达到 37.9 亿美元，这不仅创下电子游戏史上最高首发收入纪录，也大概率是娱乐史上所有创意作品中规模最大的首发。这场现象级首发展现了游戏 IP 在商业、文化以及好莱坞层面的巨大价值。 GTA6 的首发收入已经超过影史票房冠军《复仇者联盟 4：终局之战》的全球总票房 29 亿美元。 本次首发热度极高，甚至在周四改变了全球互联网流量走向。 互联网交换中心运营商 DE-CIX 称，该游戏上线催生全球数据流量新纪录。GTA6 上线时段的数据吞吐量，较今年年初常规周均值高出 25%。 Streams Charts 的数据显示，它同时创下直播观看纪录，全平台峰值在线观众 791 万人，流量主要来自 Twitch 和 YouTube。（来源：环球市场播报） 马斯克称 FSD V15 下个月将全面推送 特斯拉 CEO 伊隆·马斯克在 X 平台上发帖称，FSD V15 版本下个月将全面推送。他写道：「SFT（有监督微调）与其说是「微调」，倒不如说是「用电锯理发」！这种流程本应直接整合进基础训练阶段。而且，还要专门搞个「系统提示词」（system prompt），简直荒谬！模型默认的行为表现就该足够合理才对。上述观点在特斯拉的 AI（虽然还称不上「超级」AI）上已经得到了体现。它是目前地球上最高效的 AI。FSD V15 下个月将全面推送。它一定会带来非凡的体验。」（来源：新浪财经） 黄仁勋遭董事会罢免主要原因曝光：缺乏坦诚 两名熟悉英伟达董事长及其他董事私下讨论情况的人士透露，最终促使董事会做出决定的，是和黄仁勋「缺乏坦诚」、「撒谎」有关的多项问题。消息人士称，黄仁勋在 11 月 8 日承认存在婚外情。在随后数日，更多婚外情传闻浮出水面，其中据称包含一名直接下属。一名接近董事会的消息人士告诉《连线》：「可以确认的是，黄仁勋存在撒谎行为，该情况从 2025 年 10 月一直持续到近期事件。」知情人士表示，第一段婚外情曝光之后，董事会极为震怒。一名了解董事会想法的消息人士表示，罢免黄仁勋最主要的动因是「撒谎」。「这关乎诚信与信任。」该人士称。（来源：新浪财经） 前英特尔 CEO 基辛格：AI 需 10000 倍的效率飞跃 11 月 21 日消息，据 Wccftech 报道，前英特尔首席执行官帕特 · 基辛格（Pat Gelsinger）表示，随着人工智能需要「10,000 倍的效率飞跃」，渐进式的芯片增益将无法满足需求，他同时否认了摩尔定律已走向终结。 在 2026 年 COSM 科技峰会上，帕特 · 基辛格出席了一场题为「现实检验：超越芯片（Reality Check: Beyond Chips）」的炉边谈话。 基辛格在谈话中反驳了半导体微缩已触及物理极限的观点，他认为 AI 需要的不是常规的代际升级，而是计算效率实现激进的 10,000 倍跃升。他还指出，摩尔定律（Moore』s Law）能否重焕生机，取决于五大核心工程领域（IT 之家注：光学、供电、散热、材料和封装）的根本性突破。 峰会结束后，帕特 · 基辛格在 X 上写道：「摩尔定律已死？我说现在是唤醒它的时候了！」尽管一些行业观察人士可能会认为传统的摩尔定律微缩已经结束，但基辛格坚持认为半导体工程正在进入一个多学科创新的新时代，他表示：「在半导体行业工作 40 多年后，我相信我们最伟大的创新仍在前方！」（来源：IT 之家） Google Gemini 推出 AI 生成 GIF 功能，部分国家免费用户也可使用 Google 宣布，其人工智能助手 Gemini 现已支持用户生成自定义动画 GIF。用户只需输入简单的文字提示，或上传照片、视频作为参考，即可创建专属动态图像，无需再在 Giphy 或 Tenor 等既有 GIF 库中反复搜索合适的表情或反应图。 这项功能由 Google 近期发布的 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 视频生成模型驱动。该模型于本月早些时候推出，可生成最长 15 秒的视频片段，并具备更强的跨帧一致性和对话式编辑能力。Google 表示，新模型能够在保持画面主体及视觉细节连贯的前提下，呈现更流畅的动画效果。 根据 Google 支持文档，Gemini 生成的 GIF 长度约为 3 秒，并会以循环方式持续播放。用户可以直接在 Gemini 主聊天界面描述想要的 GIF 内容，也可以打开图片或视频创作工具，在格式选择器中选择 GIF 后输入提示词。此外，Gemini 还提供现成的 GIF 模板，帮助用户快速制作表情包或反应图，而无需从零开始设计。用户也可上传自己的图片或视频，用以定制生成结果。（来源：cnBeta） 关于混元 4 模型、算力、刷榜与 RSI，腾讯姚顺雨回应一切 11 月 21 日凌晨，腾讯首席 AI 科学家、混元大模型负责人姚顺雨和混元团队的研究员现身 Reddit LocalLLaMA 社区，开启了混元团队第一场面向全球开发者的公开 AMA。 两小时内，姚顺雨和混元团队解答了 300 余条开发者提问，从底层架构取舍到长期路线规划，从量化落地经验到开源生态适配，几乎覆盖了当前开源大模型领域所有核心争议与关切。 混元采用「两端并行」的研发策略：一边扩大模型与数据规模，探索智能上限；一边压缩推理成本，主打极致性价比，Hy4 与 Hy4 flash 分别对应这两个方向。 后续产品路线清晰，更小尺寸的 Hy4-mini、Flash-Lite 模型已在规划中；24–31B 稠密模型正在评估；5–12B 级小型开源图像模型、新一代视频模型均在考虑范围内；循环式 MoE、持续学习等前沿方向也在积极研究。 团队认为，打磨扎实的小尺寸模型同样可以胜过大参数模型，且部署成本更低，研发过程中能沉淀更多技术经验。但混元同时相信 Scaling law 的有效性，下一代模型的参数量会显著扩大，会持续向更大规模投入研发。 落到具体技术选择上，无论是注意力机制选型、MoE 稀疏度设计，还是量化方案的取舍，团队的判断都锚定实验结果、硬件适配条件与实际部署效率，并未将参数规模或榜单分数作为核心决策标准。（来源：极客公园） Nothing 首款 AI 原生硬件设备定档：无屏幕设计、预计主打会议记录用途 11 月 21 日消息，Nothing 发文，预热旗下首款 AI 原生硬件设备将于 12 月 8 日正式亮相。这款产品将采用无屏幕设计，定位为面向日常办公与生产力场景的 AI 工具。 从此前公布的预热图片来看，这款设备采用小巧的矩形机身，表面使用拉丝金属材质，并配有实体按键。其中一个面积较大的按键标有「Talk」字样，另一个按键则带有录音标识，机身上还提供红色与绿色 LED 状态指示灯，可以看出该产品预计主打会议记录用途。 title: 林俊旸新公司估值升至 50 亿美元；丁磊：短剧爆发冲击游戏产业；华为新品牌星芒发布首款阔直板手机
summary: 传林俊旸 AI 初创公司完成新融资，估值翻倍至 50 亿美元 据彭博社报道，阿里巴巴集团前 AI 负责人林俊旸创办的语用科技 ( Pragmatik Labs)，已完成新一轮融资，估值达 50 亿美元，短短几个月内估值翻了一倍多。 林俊旸曾是阿里的明星研究员，在离职后于今年夏季创立语用科技。据知情人士称，语用科技在最近结束的一轮融资中筹集了数千万美元资金。今年 8 月，该公司在首次融资中筹集了数亿美元，当时估值为 20 亿美元。 知情人士称，语用科技的新投资者包括华业天成资本、鼎晖投资以及汽车制造商吉利汽车。 语用科技总部位于上海，致力于开发面向数字世界和物理世界的 AI 智能体。该公司首轮融资的投资方包括高榕创投、红杉中国、腾讯以及上海未来产业基金。（来源：凤凰网科技） 网传张楠、谢欣将离职，本人辟谣：信息不准确 11 月 20 日午间，有媒体报道称，原抖音 CEO 张楠、原飞书 CEO 谢欣将从字节跳动离职。字节相关负责人回应称该信息不准确。 谢欣本人则在朋友圈辟谣：「媒体今天发的所谓『独家』的假新闻，浪费我大把时间去回复大家。」 值得注意的是，谢欣还将自己的微信名称改成带有「假新闻」的版本，用最直接的方式进行辟谣。（来源：新浪科技） DeepSeek 千亿级融资落地，梁文锋保留绝对控制权 工商信息显示，DeepSeek 运营主体杭州深度求索人工智能基础技术研究有限公司近日完成工商变更，新增股东杭州程砚企业管理咨询合伙企业（有限合伙）。 据证券时报援引知情交易人士消息，DeepSeek 本轮融资募资规模区间在 1000 亿元至 1055 亿元，投后估值约 6155 亿元。叠加 2026 年 6 月首轮约 510 亿元融资，市场测算其短时间内两轮累计吸纳资金将超 1500 亿元。 据测算，梁文锋直接及间接持股比例合计约 67.42%，千亿资本入场并未改变控制权归属。 据悉，作为新增股东的持股平台，杭州程砚的 31 家合伙人横跨互联网、通信运营商、芯片半导体、新能源、消费电子、汽车、家电以及头部 PE / VC，几乎把大模型商业化所需的上游算力与下游场景一次性集齐。（来源：IT之家） 网易丁磊：短剧确实会对游戏产生影响 近日，在网易 2026 年第三季度业绩电话会上，管理层被问及短剧对游戏行业的影响。网易创始人兼 CEO 丁磊坦言，短剧今年呈现爆炸式发展，对用户注意力的吸引力巨大，短期内确实会对游戏产生影响。 第三季度，网易净收入 279 亿元，同比下降 1.8%；归属于公司股东的净利润 84 亿元，同比下降约 2.5%。 作为网易最重要的收入来源，游戏业务罕见出现同比下滑，成为拖累整体营收的主要因素。网易三季度游戏及相关增值服务收入 229 亿元，同比下降 1.7%，自 2024 年三季度以来再次出现同比下降。今年前两个季度，该业务收入分别同比增长 6.9% 和 9.7%。（来源：每日经济新闻） 余承东更正：享界 V8 是 L2 辅助驾驶，开车不能睡觉 11 月 20 日，鸿蒙智行享界 V8 及星芒品牌发布会在北京举行。华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端 BG 董事长余承东在介绍享界 V8 的 L3 路测能力时，谈到了 L3 落地后的使用场景，相关表述随即在网络上引发争议。 余承东在介绍享界 V8 率先开启 120km/h L3 自动驾驶跨城高速路测时称：「L3 自动驾驶来了以后，开车就不用摸方向盘了，开车是可以睡觉的，别睡死过去就行了。20 秒还是多少秒给你唤醒就可以了。」 发布会后余承东在微博上紧急发文，修正了自己的表述。余承东表示：「今天发布会上，有几句话讲得不准确，要纠正一下。享界 V8 现在给大家用的是 L2 辅助驾驶，L3 的硬件能力已具备，但还没有开放。大家用辅助驾驶要专心开车、按要求握好方向盘。现在还是 L2 时代，大家一定要注意安全，开车不能睡觉。」（来源：界面新闻） 谷歌回应：原生安卓应用锁 2027 年发布，不支持旧版本系统 近日，谷歌在 Reddit 回帖中确认，安卓的原生应用锁无法通过 Google Play 系统更新下放到旧版本系统，旧手机要想用上，只能升级到 Android 17 QPR3。 原因在于功能本身，应用锁用到的是 Android 平台核心里的新 API，而 Play 系统更新只能换掉部分模块，碰不到这一层。这个说法来自谷歌方面负责 Android 社区的 Mishaal Rahman，他在 Reddit 回帖中解释，同一帖中给出了时间表，计划在 2027 年第一季度随 Android 17 QPR3 发布。 这套原生应用锁的使用方法是，长按应用图标，把它加入锁定列表，之后打开应用时，要先通过指纹、PIN 码、图案或密码这一关。 此前，手机厂商也曾推出「第三方应用锁」，但这类工具靠无障碍服务判断前台应用，再覆盖一层界面，被强制停止或分屏时容易失效，还会多耗一份电。（来源：快科技） 维珍银河新一代飞船首飞：载人去太空边缘，门票 85 万美元 近日，英国维珍银河新一代 Delta 级载人飞船 Apeiron（阿派隆）完成首飞，这也是该公司接替 VSS Unity 的新一代主力亚轨道载人飞行器，标志着商业太空旅游项目迈入新阶段。 这款新飞船定位高频次商业运营，设计寿命支持 500 次以上飞行任务，目标每周最多执行两次太空飞行，大幅提升发射效率，可一次性搭载 6 名乘客，飞行流程延续维珍银河经典模式。 由双机身母机 Eve 携带升空，到达高空后飞船分离，火箭发动机点火向上冲刺，抵达大约 80 多公里的太空边缘区域。 抵达高点后乘客可以短暂感受数分钟失重，透过舷窗俯瞰地球弧形轮廓，随后飞船无动力滑翔返回地面，实现重复使用。行业人士介绍，这类亚轨道飞行不会进入环绕地球的轨道，属于抵达太空边缘的短途太空体验。 维珍银河已经开放新一批席位预订，单人票价 85 万美元，相比早年 20 万-45 万美元的门票价格明显上涨，套餐包含太空岗前培训、飞行装备、太空港全套体验流程。（来源：快科技） 前 DeepSeek 研究员张博开源个人 Agent 项目，主打「零 token 费」 11 月 19 日，前 DeepSeek 研究员、Simplex AI 创始人张博（Tony Zhang）宣布开源个人 Agent Linger，号称要让 Agent 摆脱对云端数据中心的依赖，直接运行在用户自己的电脑上。项目发布后迅速引发关注，GitHub 星标数已突破 2k。

title: 估值 410 亿美元，贝佐斯打造「物理世界的 OpenAI」
summary: 作者｜宇航猿 编辑｜靖宇 AI 吞掉了软件，现在，它要吞掉工业了。 卸任亚马逊 CEO 五年后，杰夫·贝佐斯没忍住，又给自己找了个班上。 当地时间 2026 年 11 月 17 日，加州门洛帕克的 Semafor「硅谷与世界」峰会现场，贝佐斯和物理学家维克·巴贾杰（Vik Bajaj）罕见同台。 他现在的最新头衔，是 AI 初创公司 Prometheus 的联合创始人兼联席 CEO 。这是自 2021 年交出亚马逊帅印后，这位商业巨头首次重回一线担任 CEO。 早在 2024 年底种子期就掏钱投资的贝佐斯，在台上毫不掩饰自己的兴奋，直言项目进展太快，自己根本「没法坐在场边干看着」。 能让贝佐斯重返战场的，是个大赌局。 点开 Prometheus 的官网首页，目前只有极简的品牌标识与暖色光晕背景，几乎看不到任何公开的产品细节。但在水面之下， 这家仅有约 250 名员工的神秘公司，估值已经飙升至 410 亿美元，累计筹集了约 145 亿美元资金 。 极度低调的 Prometheus 官网首页目前仅展示品牌标识，尚未向公众开放工具集｜图片来源：Prometheus 官网 在长达 32 分钟的对谈里，贝佐斯第一次掀开了底牌。以往需要 10 到 20 人的工程师团队，耗时 6 到 9 个月才能搞定的模拟芯片、无线电设备或阀门设计，Prometheus 的系统在 12 小时内就能做完。他名下的商业航天公司蓝色起源，已经在两个项目上私密内测这套工具。 硅谷还在为聊天机器人和写代码的智能体卷生卷死，贝佐斯直接换了一张牌桌。 Prometheus 的野心，是成为物理世界的 OpenAI，用「原子的 AI」， 去重构数十万亿美元的实体制造业。 01 牛顿造不出小烤箱 Prometheus 145 亿美元的融资规模，很多人的第一反应，是贝佐斯也要下场造人形机器人了。 他在峰会上直接否认了这个猜测——Prometheus 既不做陪聊的语言模型，也不造双足机器人， 它的终极目标是打造「通用 AI 工程师」（Artificial General Engineer，简称 AGE） 。 为什么今天无所不能的纯文本大语言模型，干不了硬核工程师的活？ 贝佐斯在现场抛出了一个非常形象的比喻，「光靠阅读学不会工程。就算我读一千本体操书，我依然是个糟糕的体操运动员；读一千本舞蹈书，我还是不会跳舞。」 贝佐斯说，把牛顿、爱因斯坦和麦克斯韦等六位顶尖物理学家关进同一间屋子，让他们造一台小烤箱，这群天才大概率会毫无头绪。理解麦克斯韦方程组对造小烤箱毫无帮助， 因为理论物理和工程制造， 是在完全不同的颗粒度上运作的 。 曾任 Google X 核心高管、斯坦福大学医学院教授的联席 CEO 巴贾杰补充了另一个现实。哪怕在纯语言模型领域，专业化分工也已经不可避免，比如 Anthropic 能在编程能力上领先，正是源于高度专注。而到了物理世界，哪怕是手机里一个不起眼的无线电模块，不仅需要几十年的人类工程积淀，还得同时精通热学、力学和电磁特性才能完成封装。传统工程里，光是设置一次物理仿真往往就要耗费几天到几周。 为了跨越这道鸿沟， Prometheus 避开了纯文本路线，底层直接构建了用于数值仿真的神经代理模型， 和统一的多物理场模型，做成由 AI 驱动的新一代 CAD、物理仿真与工程智能体 。 这种跨学科能力，在内部测试中展现出了惊人的直觉。团队里有一位曾参与 NASA 喷气推进实验室（JPL）火星直升机研发的工程师，试着只用一句提示词，让系统重新设计火星直升机。 面对火星极端恶劣的环境，模型在庞大的设计空间里自主权衡。它先后比对了四旋翼、共轴反桨直升机与固定翼方案，最终收敛到与真实火星直升机高度相似的共轴反桨构型，还针对火星稀薄大气算出桨叶弦长等参数、自动生成需求指标，遇到意图不清时甚至会主动反问工程师。 NASA 机智号火星直升机概念图，曾参与该项目的工程师用一句提示词便让 Prometheus 重新推导出高度相似的共轴反桨构型｜图片来源：NASA/JPL-Caltech 要啃下这种硬骨头，光靠写代码的算法天才远远不够，Prometheus 攒出了一支 极端混搭 的 250 人「 梦之队 」。 人工智能的人手，他们从 OpenAI、Google DeepMind、Meta 和微软挖来大批顶尖研究员。xAI 联合创始人、曾主导马斯克 Colossus 超算建设的 Kyle Kosic 在 summary: 「史上最大 IPO」：Anthropic 上市首日收盘大涨 17%，市值达 1.27 万亿美元 11 月 20 日消息，AI 公司 Anthropic 于当地时间 11 月 19 日在美国纳斯达克上市， 首日股价以 97.17 美元（现汇率约合 649.2 元人民币）收盘，较 83 美元（现汇率约合 554.5 元人民币）的发行价上涨 17.07%。 该股开盘即报 111.5 美元（现汇率约合 744.9 元人民币），较发行价高出约 34.3%；盘中一度突破 115 美元（现汇率约合 768.3 元人民币），随后回落至 100 美元（现汇率约合 668.1 元人民币）下方。 按收盘价计算，Anthropic 市值约为 1.27 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.48 万亿元人民币），成为全球最受关注的 AI 公司之一。不过，其每股收益为 -59.62 美元（现汇率约合 -398.3 元人民币），意味着公司仍处于高投入、尚未实现稳定盈利的阶段；市场目前更多是在为 AI 基础模型、企业级应用及未来商业化能力定价。 按照「IPO 募资额」计算，Anthropic 本次上市募资 813 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,431.47 亿元人民币），超过了 SpaceX 今年 6 月的 750 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,010.58 亿元人民币），成为有史以来最大规模的公开市场首次募股。（来源：IT 之家） 苹果正自研 AI 智能体：可操控设备、浏览网页、编写代码，以期与 OpenAI、Anthropic 竞争 11 月 20 日消息，彭博社马克 · 古尔曼（Mark Gurman）今日报道称，苹果正在开发自主 AI 智能体，计划让 AI 代替用户执行设备操控、应用操作、网页浏览和软件编程等任务，进一步进入由 OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta 等公司参与竞争的 AI 智能体市场。 古尔曼发现，苹果已经在官网发布招聘信息，其中一份职位招聘面向高级工程经理，岗位名称为「主动式智能体 AI」（Agentic AI - Proactive）。招聘信息称，苹果正在组建团队开发能够代表用户执行任务的 AI 助手，相关系统将具备编写代码、浏览网页、控制应用程序以及操作设备等能力。苹果在招聘信息中描述了未来 AI 智能体的工作方式：用户可以让 AI 像熟练的人类操作者一样使用电脑，在浏览器、文档、终端、代码编辑器和各类服务之间切换，自主选择合适的工具完成任务。 该系统不仅能够执行单一指令，还可以规划并完成跨应用、浏览器、命令行和 API 的多步骤任务，同时协调多个专门负责不同工作的子智能体。苹果还特别强调隐私保护，称这类能够运行代码、使用用户凭据并代表用户采取行动的智能体，需要具备严格的权限管理、沙盒隔离和操作透明度。 不过，项目目前仍处于早期开发阶段，古尔曼表示，苹果新任 CEO 约翰 · 特努斯（John Ternus）一直在推动软件工程负责人克雷格 · 费德里吉（Craig Federighi）加快 AI 开发进度，并采取更加积极的策略。自主 AI 智能体被视为苹果推进这一战略的重要组成部分。（来源：IT 之家） 蚂蚁集团上半年利润增长 17%，将持续投入 AI 11 月 19 日晚间消息，阿里巴巴发布 2026 年三季度财报。财报显示，2026 年上半年，阿里从蚂蚁获得的收益为 50.23 亿元；据此推算蚂蚁集团 2026 年上半年利润约为 152 亿元，同比增加约 17%。 技术底座侧，蚂蚁 CEO 韩歆毅曾表示，希望为 AI 大规模落地提供支付、数据、安全等底座能力。支付宝已推出全栈 AI 支付体系，为 Agent 商业生态提供支付和结算设施 OceanBase 推出湖库一体的 AI 数据平台，被视为其从「分布式数据库」向「AI 时代数据智能底座」的全面升级。 应用侧，公开信息显示，蚂蚁阿福累计服务用户已超 1.5 亿，规模在全球同类健康管理 AI 应用中领先；蚂蚁数科推出「智能体超级工厂」方案，以 Agentar 平台为核心，面向企业提供智能体规模化生产、管理和运营能力。前沿布局上，通过蚂蚁灵波科技切入具身智能赛道，其具身原生机器人通用大脑已在智慧药房、物流、工业等多个场景落地。 与此同时，蚂蚁的 AI 能力也在走向海外，蚂蚁国际在全球服务约 20 亿消费者，覆盖超过 220 个国家和地区，为其 AI 应用的跨区域复用提供了基本盘。（来源：新浪科技） 阿里巴巴 CEO 吴泳铭：千问已在平头哥芯片训练下一代模型，百炼基于国产芯片提供模型推理服务 据财联社今日报道，在 2027 财年第二季度财报分析师电话会上，阿里巴巴集团 CEO 吴泳铭表示， 千问已经在平头哥芯片上训练下一代模型，百炼已经基于国产芯片提供模型推理服务 。 吴泳铭强调， 阿里的全栈 AI 基础设施将在国产算力供应链上形成明显优势 ，而自研芯片与自研模型的深度协同，将持续转化为更优的单位算力成本和更高的 AI 应用研发效率。 据 I 本月早些时候报道，全新一代千问大模型 Qwen4 即将发布：知识理解更深入，世界感知更立体，Coding 与 Agentic 能力持续进阶。现在，Qwen4-Max 预览版已首发上线阿里 Token Plan，限时最低 1 折即可体验 Qwen4 模型。 另外，阿里巴巴在港交所公告称，香港联交所已确认公司可进行建议分拆。2026 年

title: 「北美大豆包」谷歌，终于杀回 AI 牌桌中央
summary: 作者｜Wildcard 编辑｜靖宇 谷歌，这次是真的回来了。 11 月 18 日，Google DeepMind 点亮了 Gemini 4 Neon 的霓虹灯牌。 这是 Gemini 4 系列在短短 7 周内甩出的第 4 款元素模型 。如果看一眼官方放出的基准跑分长表和社区实测反馈，你会发现它精准卡在了一个极其舒服的「甜点」位上，既有接近、甚至局部反超旗舰的硬核智商，又把单任务成本砍到了竞争对手的一半左右。 在 Reddit 技术社区里，挑剔的开发者们罕见地给出了一边倒的好评，直呼它「 便宜得离谱又强得可怕 」。每月花 19.99 美元订阅 Google AI Pro 的普通用户更是喜出望外，不用咬牙上 Ultra 档位，就能在 Gemini App 里直接用上准旗舰水准的模型。加上整个 11 月密集落地的模型与工具矩阵，那个曾经在牌桌边缘徘徊的谷歌 AI，终于重新杀回了牌桌中央。 唯一让全球程序员一头雾水的，大概只有谷歌神秘的命名学。从 9 月底的 Argon（氩）、10 月底的 Carbon（碳），到 11 月中旬的 Hydrogen（氢）和如今的 Neon（氖），既不按原子序数排，也不按字母表或能力强弱分。 Hacker News 上真有较真的网友把化学性质全列出来找规律，最后绝望地吐槽谷歌大概是把元素扔进帽子里随机抓出来的，用星巴克杯型命名都比这清楚；国内网友则已经开始催更第 118 号元素「鿫」（Oganesson），顺便调侃看个科技新闻还得重背初中化学。 网友为 Gemini 4 设计的「元素周期表」选模型界面｜图片来源：网络 01 炼金术「杰作」 名字虽然让人摸不着头脑，但 Neon 在产品矩阵里的刀法却异常清晰。 它精准卡在重型长周期旗舰 Carbon，与轻量高频执行模型 Hydrogen 之间，直接取代了此前 Gemini 3.1 Pro 和 Argon 的生态位。Alphabet 首席科学家兼 DeepMind 董事长 Demis Hassabis 给它的评价颇高，称其为「炼金术的杰作」。 支撑这句评价的是实打实的硬指标。Neon 拥有 100 万 token 的上下文窗口（在 Antigravity 中支持最高 512K 上下文）和最高 100 万 token 的输出上限，支持文本、音视频、PDF 及电子表格的原生多模态输入。在核心推理能力上，它提供了 low、medium、high（默认）和 xhigh 四档可调思考深度，给了开发者极大的控本空间。 独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 的数据最能说明问题。在 AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 总榜上， Neon 开启 xhigh 档位拿下了 61 分，高居全球第三，排在 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5.2 之后 ，把自家老大哥 Carbon 的 high 档（60 分）、Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5（59 分）以及 OpenAI 的 GPT-6.2 Sol（57 分）全都压在了身下。即便切回默认的 high 档也能拿 60 分，而降到 medium 档拿到的 55 分，依然超过了轻量模型 Hydrogen 拼尽全力的 xhigh 档（54 分）。 真正让企业客户心动的，是那张跑分与单任务成本的散点折线图。 Neon 把一线旗舰的智商，打出了中端走量模型的账单。 它的输出速度达到每秒约 110 tokens，接近 Carbon（约 57 tokens/s）的两倍；跑完 AA 基准单任务的平均耗时从 Carbon 的 36 分钟缩短到 21.5 分钟，单任务成本定格在 6.44 美元，比恢复标准价后的 Carbon（7.76 美元）低了约 17%。在 Antigravity 平台的默认 high 档下，单次任务成本更是比 Carbon 直接砍掉了 32%。 AA Index v5.0.1 下 Gemini 4 Neon 各档位与 Carbon、Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol 的智力分与单任务成本对比｜图片来源：Google 把目光转到当下最卷的编程与企业级赛道，这种性价比杀伤力更加直观。在 AA Coding Agent Index 榜单上，Neon 以 58.6

title: [AINews] Riemann Hypothesis proved...twice independently
summary: Within a few hours of each other ( timeline ), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics ( Scientific American ). Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. So if it finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, and no human will ever have read all of it… …prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human , work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett ). This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim is still the cautionary tale: critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
summary: The word of the year in the AI industry over 2026 has been “slop” — meaning low-quality output from a large language model. And with so much code being AI-generated now, avoiding slop has become a daily concern for software engineers. So how to do that? One way is to use formal verification systems , which use mathematical proofs and logic to verify the correctness of software or hardware. With AI’s growing prowess at solving math problems , there’s now a number of AI companies offering formal verification systems. They include Harmonic , Theorem , Axiom Math , and a new entrant called &Truth (pronounced ‘and truth’). In this article we’ll look at some of the approaches these companies are taking. How formal verification is used in software and AI today In order to better understand the landscape of formal verification systems, we spoke to one of its leading proponents: Clark Barrett , &Truth’s co-founder and co-CEO. He’s also Corbel Professor (Research) of Computer Science at Stanford and was the co-creator of cvc5 , a popular automated reasoning engine used in formal verification. title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
summary: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20 . Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s'); SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama'; The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch

title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
summary: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. summary: By David Spreng The financing of the AI buildout is shifting from equity to debt, and those who invested through the telecom bubble may recognize what that shift tends to mean. There is an old story in Stephen Hawking ’s “A Brief History of Time” about a scientist lecturing on the universe when a woman in the audience insists that the world rests on the back of a giant turtle. Asked what the turtle stands on, she replies that it’s “turtles all the way down.” Her response is what philosophers call infinite regress — a chain of claims in which each one rests on another of the same kind and solid ground never arrives. David Spreng is the founder, co-CEO and co-CIO of Runway Growth Capital. I think of it when I look at the AI buildout because its logic has taken the same shape. Valuations support borrowing, and borrowing builds capacity. The capacity then becomes proof that the valuations were right, so each claim stands on the one beneath it. title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
summary: By Richard Anton Panics and pile-ons are a familiar pattern in the public markets, with a herd mentality wiping value from companies in an instant. Trading can swiftly become a barometer of emotions, rather than a well-informed gauge of value. We have seen this play out with AI’s impact on software companies and the supposed end of the Software as a Service business model. The doom-laden talk of the SaaSpocalypse was noise, with little signal, and most traders were initially unable to distinguish between a company that will thrive in the AI age and one that will be decimated by it. The SaaSpocalypse didn’t reveal the end of software. It revealed the limits of public markets in judging its value. This pattern erodes trust in the public markets. For companies, being publicly owned may no longer be appealing, and founders considering an exit may not view an initial public offering as the ultimate goal. summary: Paul Graham, the Y Combinator co-founder, said the two young Irish entrepreneurs reminded him of Patrick and John Collison, the Irish brothers who founded and run the $160bn payment giant Stripe. Ryan Morrissey and Bence Redmond, the co-founders of AI startup Hoplite , might not be brothers but, like the Collison brothers, are Irish, have ties to Limerick, and attended Y Combinator. title: OakNorth wins US banking licence
summary: OakNorth , the UK SME lender, has won a US banking licence, it said today, allowing it to offer services beyond lending including checking and savings accounts to businesses in the US, which now accounts for 40 per cent of its lending business. The digital bank, which is backed by Japanese investor SoftBank and GIC, the Singaporean state fund, said it’s the first foreign digital bank to secure a US banking licence, after winning regulatory approval from the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. OakNorth applied for US regulatory approval through its acquisition of Community Unity Bank , an FDIC-insured lender in Michigan, which it acquired in 2025. Earlier this year, the Federal Reserve told OakNorth to move its domicile from Jersey to the UK to clear its purchase of Community Unity Bank. The UK challenger bank, which launched in the UK in 2015 and has lent over $24bn, first entered the US market in 2023 and has provided $3.5bn in lending to American businesses. title: Archer raises $10M to connect recruiters and job seekers with AI
summary: Archer (formerly hackajob) has raised $10 million in new funding in a round led by Volition Capital , with participation from existing investor AVP . The company develops an AI-powered recruiting platform designed to connect employers with suitable candidates while helping job seekers discover relevant opportunities. Founded by Mark Chaffey and Razvan Creanga at King’s College London, hackajob initially operated as a reverse hiring marketplace where companies applied to software engineers. The platform grew to one million users before the company began developing Archer in 2025, adapting its approach to the growing use of AI in recruitment. Developed in collaboration with customer Sainsbury’s and publicly launched in September, Archer uses AI to automate candidate sourcing, qualification and introductions. Unlike recruitment tools focused primarily on employers or job seekers, the platform serves both sides, recommending candidates to recruiters and relevant positions to applicants. The growing use of AI in recruitment is changing the dynamics of the hiring process, creating new challenges for both employers and job seekers. As AI tools simplify job applications, application volumes have tripled, while the average likelihood of securing an interview has declined from approximately 15 per cent to 2 per cent. title: Ukrainian drone engineering meets German manufacturing as QFI ramps up production
summary: Quantum Systems and Frontline Robotics are expanding their industrial cooperation through a programme for long-term support capacity in Ukraine aimed at systems developed by Frontline Robotics and produced in Germany by Quantum Frontline Industries (QFI). The programme is the next stage of the partnership the two companies established in December 2025 through (QFI), their joint venture for manufacturing Ukrainian-developed unmanned systems at scale. QFI plans to expand its production capacity fivefold in 2027. “The additional commitment represents a further step to strengthen Ukraine’s domestic defence-industrial base and build long-term capacity to support Ukrainian-developed unmanned systems. Through QFI, we’ve shown what Ukrainian engineering and German manufacturing can achieve together. title: EU–INC calls on von der Leyen to withdraw and re-table EU Inc proposal
summary: EU–INC and Startups for Europe are calling on European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to withdraw and re-table the original EU Inc proposal, warning that compromises made by EU Member States threaten to undermine one of Europe’s most important economic reforms for startups and scaleups. The announcement comes as Europe’s leading policymakers, founders and investors gather at Slush in Helsinki to discuss the state of EU Inc. After two years of campaigning for a single European company standard, EU–INC and Startups for Europe remain strong supporters of the European Commission’s original proposal. The Commission delivered a solid framework that could finally give European founders a genuine alternative to incorporating in Delaware, and allow companies to start and scale under one common European standard. But the Council’s negotiating mandate of 19 October has weakened or removed some of the very provisions that would make EU Inc a true European standard: Free choice of registration – Weakened: Founders can choose where to incorporate, but national authorities have more room to challenge that choice in certain circumstances, creating legal uncertainty. title: €100B in company value, one shared ambition: European tech leaders demand political reform at Slush
summary: More than 35 European tech founders and business leaders issued a joint declaration at Slush 2026, calling for three fundamental shifts in European technology policy to strengthen the continent's global competitiveness. Representing more than €100 billion in company value and 115,000 jobs, the signatories pledged their long-term commitment to building and scaling technology companies in Europe. “We share one conviction: Europe can lead the next era of technology, and we want to make it happen.” The declaration challenges the prevailing narrative of European decline, pointing to the continent's scientific excellence, private wealth and strengths in advanced manufacturing, energy, aerospace, robotics, quantum, climate technology and AI. The EU accounts for around 22 per cent of global scientific publications, compared with 17 per cent for the US, according to the declaration. Yet Europe has struggled to translate these strengths into global technology leadership. “Europe was never short of talent, technology or capital. It was short of the political determination and the boldness to put them to work.” The signatories identify three political priorities to address this imbalance. title: Wallenberg Investments takes minority stake in Swedish deeptech Algoryx
summary: The investment unit of the Wallenberg family, one of Sweden’s most prominent financial dynasties, has taken a minority stake in Swedish deeptech company Algoryx , the company said today. Wallenberg Investments has taken an undisclosed minority shareholding in Algoryx, the company said. Algoryx develops software that simulates how robots and heavy machinery behave in the real world, generating synthetic data to train the AI that controls autonomous machines. Algoryx has built technology for physics simulation and software tools for machine manufacturers, robotics companies, industrial customers and space projects across Europe, North America and Asia. It was founded in 2007 as a spin-off from Sweden’s Umeå University. The new funds will be used to expand its team, increase compute capacity, and speed up AI research and the development of its next-generation product platform. Algoryx’s founders and employees remain the majority owners of the company. Alex Basu, Head of Ventures at Wallenberg Investments. “Algoryx combines deep expertise in physics simulation with close industrial relationships. The investment therefore fits squarely within our focus on backing technology leaders to drive industrial renewal and competitiveness in Europe.”

summary: London-based AI drug discovery startup Boltz has raised a $110m Series A funding round, less than a year after emerging out of stealth. Boltz is an AI research startup that develops AI models to speed up drug discovery. It was spun out of MIT in the US but is now located in London, employing 40 AI researchers in the capital's King's Cross district. Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, with existing investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Amplify Partners, Zetta Venture Partners and Obvious Ventures participating. New investors include Greycroft, F-Prime Capital, Hummingbird and Benchling, joining Nvidia, which also announced an investment earlier this year during Jensen Huang’s visit to the UK . It follows Boltz raising a $28m seed round at the start of the year. The startup builds software which helps pharmaceutical and biotech researchers design potential drugs and decide which candidates to test in labs. Its AI models can predict what protein and drug candidates look like when bound together, estimate how strongly they bind, and propose new molecules designed to bind to a target. title: Wilgot raises $3M in seed funding to help brands get recommended by AI
summary: Stockholm-based startup Wilgot , which develops technology to help brands improve their product visibility in AI assistants, has raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by Industrifonden . The round also included participation from Luminar Ventures, Foundry Ventures, Ventures Together and Inovexus, alongside angel investors Johan Bäckarlin and Johan Hjelte, founders of Voyado, and Niclas Mollin, founder of inriver and Occtoo. Founded in 2024 by Erik Wikander (CEO), Dr Mhairi Dunion (AI Scientist) and Oleg Danylenko (CTO), Wilgot helps brands adapt their product information to changing consumer shopping behaviour. Consumers are increasingly using AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Perplexity to discover products and receive shopping recommendations. Rather than searching for specific items, users can describe their needs in natural language and receive suggestions based on their preferences. This shift is changing how brands reach potential customers, as traditional product descriptions and marketing content may not provide AI assistants with the information needed to recommend relevant products. title: LATO secures $4.7M to automate customer and expert interviews with AI
summary: AI-powered market research platform LATO has raised $4.7 million in a seed funding round co-led by Air Street Capital and Axiom Partners . Its backers also include Y Combinator, Montis VC and Inception Fund, alongside angel investors including Paul Graham and co-founders of ElevenLabs, Vercel, Snowflake and Rogo. Founded by Tymek Staniszewski and Tien Chu , LATO develops AI agents that conduct customer and industry expert interviews to help investment firms assess businesses, markets and growth opportunities. Before investing in a company, private equity firms conduct commercial due diligence to assess its market position, customer relationships and growth potential. While financial data provides insights into revenue and retention, understanding purchasing decisions and competitive pressures often requires direct conversations with customers across different markets. LATO aims to streamline this process through AI agents that identify and interview customers and industry experts in their own languages. The platform combines insights from these conversations with published research and investors' internal data to help assess market conditions, competitive positioning and business assumptions. title: Noah raises €800K to help companies unlock their AI potential
summary: Antwerp-based startup Noah , which develops an AI-powered platform to help companies identify and prioritise opportunities for artificial intelligence adoption, has raised €800,000 from a group of business angels. Investors include Rudi Deruytter, former CEO of B-Bank, entrepreneur Ben Schrauwen and Nicolas Debray of Belgium Startup Ecosystem. The financing is supplemented by subsidies and a bank loan. Founded by Denis Leysen (CEO), César Van Leuffelen (CPO) and Tom De Smedt (CTO), Noah helps businesses assess where AI can deliver value by analysing internal processes, identifying potential use cases and estimating their financial impact. While companies increasingly recognise the potential of AI, many struggle to identify where to begin or how to measure its benefits. According to Denis Leysen, CEO and co-founder of Noah, traditional approaches such as hiring consultants or assigning internal teams can be costly and time-consuming, creating demand for faster ways to evaluate AI opportunities. Noah addresses this challenge through an AI interviewer that conducts 20-minute conversations with employees in multiple languages to identify opportunities for automation and process improvements. According to the company, the platform can complete up to 100 interviews within 24 hours, compared with the month a consultant would typically need to conduct 20 interviews.

title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M to bring health monitoring from smartphones to humanoid robots
summary: Belgian healthtech company IntelliProve has raised €2.7 million in a seed funding round led by Miles Ahead , with participation from Wit-Gele Kruis , imec.istart and several business angels. IntelliProve develops software that enables standard cameras in smartphones, laptops and other devices to measure health indicators without requiring additional equipment or physical contact. Through a 30-second facial scan, the technology provides six biomarkers: heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), respiratory rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and resonant breathing. Healthcare systems face growing pressure from ageing populations, staff shortages and rising demand for care. Traditional health monitoring often requires dedicated equipment and professional assistance, making these services harder to scale. IntelliProve aims to address this by enabling users to measure vital signs remotely through cameras in everyday devices. The company's technology uses remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) to detect subtle changes in skin colour caused by blood circulation and movements associated with breathing. Its software processes these signals to estimate health indicators, using proprietary technologies designed to improve measurement accuracy across different lighting conditions, movements and cameras.
